newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to get U.S. choppers for drug war.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to get U.S. choppers for drug war.

text.p: Mexico on Tuesday said it expected to obtain 53 U.S. military helicopters next year to help it combat drugs, a sharp increase from the 20 in the process of being delivered this year.

Following an announcement by U.S. President Bill Clinton that he would give $112 million of military equipment and training to Latin American countries to help stop the flow of drugs, the Mexican Foreign Ministry said their share would be $37 million.

That includes 53 UH-1H helicopters, spare parts and their transit to Mexico, worth $25 million, and four C-26 Fairchild observation aircraft worth $12 million. It said the aid needed U.S. Congressional approval.

"This equipment will enable our armed institution to mobilise personnel rapidly, efficiently and safely to zones of difficult access to eradicate crops of illicit products," a Foreign Ministry statement said.

The White House announced the supplies in New York, where Clinton on Tuesday attended the U.N. General Assembly. He has been accused by Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole of taking a lax attitude toward drug control in America.

Mexico has long counted on U.S. support to fight dug traffickers, who ship large quantities of South American cocaine via Mexico to the United States. Heroin and marijuana are also produced in Mexico.
